title: Fireside Demo Critique & Positioning Lab
topics: How to pitch Dedicated vs Hosted
summary: Internal SE/AE enablement: critique of a live demo recording, practice competitive positioning vs major providers, and refine messaging for Dedicated vs Hosted options. Agreed next steps include updated battlecards, a canned opening script, and a short recording for public examples.
next_steps: Elena to circulate revised demo script by 2025-03-21
Marco to produce a 3-min trimmed demo clip for enablement library by 2025-03-24
Aisha to update competitive battlecard with latency and cost talking points by 2025-03-22
Jordan to run 2 mock calls with the new script and report back 2025-03-28
action_items: Elena Ortiz: Draft crisp 60s intro + 2 callouts (privacy + SLOs) - due 2025-03-21
Marco Chen: Export demo clip with captions and error highlights - due 2025-03-24
Aisha Patel: Revise battlecard and share in sales slack - due 2025-03-22
Ravi Singh: Provide two sentences on product roadmap/Private deployment nuance - due 2025-03-25
transcript:
Header: Tue Mar 18 2025 14:30 PST | Duration: 75 mins
Attendees: Aisha Patel (AE), Marco Chen (SE), Elena Ortiz (SE Trainer), Ravi Singh (PM), Jordan Blake (Field AE), Priya Malhotra (Enablement)
Recording link: https://redwood.internal/enablement/recordings/ff-20250318-ef6b (internal)

[00:00] Aisha: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining the fireside demo critique. We're going to watch the clip and then do two rounds of live roleplay. Quick goals: tighten the opening, surface the dedicated vs hosted talk earlier, and weaponize the latency/cost rebuttal. Elena, you wanna kick us off?

[00:22] Elena: Yeah just a couple housekeeping things. This is low pressure, call it practice. If you interrupt me, feel free, it's supposed to be noisy. Marco recorded a 12 minute demo last week that we'll play back. I've flagged three moments where the flow stumbled.

[00:39] Marco: Quick note, the clip has some background noise - mic wasn't great - so transcription will look weird in parts. Also I trimmed the VM responses to keep it tight.

[00:52] Jordan: Sounds good. I also sent my notes in the doc, so if anyone cross references, it's in the enablement folder.

[01:05] (clip plays - audio playback)
[02:30] Speaker 1 (clip): "...and so with Redwood you get predictable token costs and we handle the heavy lifting for you so you don't need to hire infra engineers to, uh, glue everything together..."

[03:04] Aisha: Pause. Elena?

[03:07] Elena: Yeah that was the first stumble. 'We handle the heavy lifting' is vague. We want to say specifically what we own — runtime, autoscaling, KV cache management — so the buyer hears technical depth. Also tie it to customer's job-to-be-done: reduce engineering headcount or time-to-market.

[03:35] Marco: I had meant to say runtime but it came out fluffy. I'll mark that.

[03:40] Priya: Small thing - when you say 'predictable token costs' buyers sometimes hear 'expensive but stable'. Maybe lead with 'cost controls and optimizations' then call out batching/caching.

[03:55] Aisha: Good — so: 'cost controls' then example. Ravi, where would you put quantization/optimizer in that sentence?

[04:05] Ravi: Short answer: put it after the sentence about batching and caching. Eg: 'We reduce unit cost via batching, KV prefix caching and model quantization options.' Keep jargon lean but specific.

[04:20] (clip resumes)
[05:10] Speaker 1 (clip): "...if latency is a concern, we can move you to Dedicated which gives you pinned GPU and guaranteed throughput..."

[05:28] Aisha: That felt late in the demo. Jordan?

[05:31] Jordan: Yeah, you need to surface the Dedicated vs Hosted trade earlier — ideally in the 'What we solve' slide — because enterprise buyers want to know options immediately. People stop listening if they think there's no on-prem path.

[05:46] Elena: Also how you phrase it matters. Avoid binary 'move you to' language. Instead: 'You can choose Hosted for rapid rollout or Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation.' Then a one-liner on Private for regulated stuff.

[06:05] Marco: I stumbled when asked about SLOs — I said 'we have SLAs' and they pressed for numbers. I didn't have them on hand.

[06:12] Priya: Tip: have a cheat-sheet with SLA numbers (p99 latency, uptime) and a canned fallback story: 'if you need lower latency we can pair with a smaller model variant or deploy in a closer region.'

[06:30] Aisha: Let's roleplay that question. Jordan, you're the skeptical infra lead. How would you ask?

[06:36] Jordan (roleplay): "We've got tight p99 requirements, sub-50ms on some flows — can you hit that and what happens if you don't?"

[06:42] Marco (roleplay): "Uh, yes, we can— well, our Dedicated offering gives pinned GPUs and we have autoscaling to…"

[06:50] Elena (interrupt): Stop. That's reactive. Better: "We operate Dedicated pools with latency SLOs, typical p99s on this model family are X–Y ms in our benchmarks; if you exceed that we have automatic fallbacks to lower-latency model variants plus region failover. We'll also provide tracing and token-level latency dashboards in the Console."

[07:18] Aisha: That felt stronger. Make the 'we will provide' concrete — mention tracing hooks and token-level dashboards. Buyers like measurable promises.

[07:27] (clip - demo shows a code example)
[08:05] Speaker 1 (clip): "...and here's how you call the API, it's super simple, SDKs for JS, Python..."

[08:15] Priya: I called out that you glossed over rate limiting and quotas which some customers hit early. Maybe mention 'rate limiting and quotas' plus 'can set per-route limits' as part of the operational narrative.

[08:29] Marco: Would saying 'per-route quotas' confuse non-engineering buyers?

[08:33] Elena: Keep the terms, but offer a short explanation: 'per-route quotas let you protect high-value endpoints — e.g., customer-facing chat — while allowing internal batch jobs to scale.'

[08:49] Aisha: Cool. Let's jump to competitive rebuttals — common objection: 'OpenAI is cheaper and faster.' What do we want reps to say?

[08:58] Jordan: Quick script: 'OpenAI gives a broad hosted offering; our edge is predictable economics at scale, richer observability, and enterprise controls like VPC/Private deploys and audit logs.'

[09:12] Marco: People also attack us on model quality — "but OpenAI models are better." How do we answer?

[09:18] Elena: We acknowledge parity in some tasks, then pivot: 'We enable you to choose and pin model versions, run A/B rollouts, and quickly swap to a different variant if you detect regressions; our Optimize tooling gives quantization and model recommendations tuned to your workload.'

[09:37] Aisha: That worked. Now let's do two live runs: Jordan will play buyer, Aisha will run. After each run we'll annotate, then Marco will try.

[09:45] (Roleplay 1 begins)
[10:00] Jordan (roleplay): "We're evaluating a chat product, our SLAs are strict, and engineering is small. What's your cost model?"

[10:08] Aisha (roleplay): "We bill by tokens for Hosted with built-in batching and caching to reduce unit cost. For predictable throughput and isolation we recommend Dedicated which is reserved capacity and helps with sustained p99s. We also provide tooling to right-size the config so you can save on GPUs without sacrificing latency."

[10:28] Jordan (roleplay): "Okay but is Dedicated just more expensive?"

[10:32] Aisha (roleplay): "It's a different economic trade-off: you trade commit for predictability. With our Optimize recommendations you often save on total run cost by enabling quantization and batching. We can share examples from customers who reduced per-token costs by 30% after tuning."

[10:50] Jordan: Good cadence. Two notes: one—specific customer numbers help. Two—don't overpromise '30%' without naming the workload.

[11:00] Elena: Right, say 'in similar retrieval-heavy gen workloads we've seen up to ~30% reduction' or 'customer X saw...'. If you can anonymize, great.

[11:12] Marco: I'm going to try the demo now but shorter, 5 minutes. Please stop me with red cards.

[11:20] (clip/playback of Marco's shortened demo)
[12:05] Speaker 2 (clip): "...and there's a dashboard where you can drill into tokens and see spike alerts which tie back to prompts..."

[12:20] Aisha: Nice visual there. Could call out the 'regression alerts' feature explicitly — ties to quality monitoring.

[12:28] Marco: I forgot to mention 'prompt set based regression alerts' — I need a crisp line for that.

[12:33] Elena: Suggested line: 'We support prompt-set based evals so you get regression alerts if quality drifts after a model change.' Simple.

[12:44] Jordan: Also, practice shorter demos. The buyer gets lost in the middle if you dive too far into SDK code. Save the deep dive for an SE session.

[12:55] Aisha: Agree. Keep the demo to a narrative: 1) problem, 2) demo, 3) outcomes and next steps.

[13:10] (crosstalk)
[13:18] Priya: Quick ask for slide updates — can we add a one-pager that maps buyer persona to the one-liner? E.g., Product: 'fast A/B cycles', Platform: 'latency SLOs + region controls'.

[13:29] Elena: Yes — we'll add a persona overlay.

[13:33] Aisha: Okay let's close with the rebuttal cheat-sheet. I'll read a couple and you call out tweaks. First: 'We can't match OpenAI's R&D — so why Redwood?'

[13:44] Jordan: Response: 'OpenAI invests in base models; Redwood invests in serving and operational control — we make model inference predictable and auditable for production apps.'

[13:55] Marco: Could add 'and we make it economical via batching and model recommendations' to the end.

[14:05] Elena: Another common objection: 'We host ourselves to keep data private.' Reply: 'We offer Private deployments with a customer-managed control plane and on-prem options; we integrate with KMS/HSM and provide audit logs.'

[14:19] Aisha: Ok that lands. We're at 14:20 in the session — about an hour left. Quick lightning round: each of you give one thing to change in the deck/demo. Marco?

[14:28] Marco: Reduce the code sample size, move SLA numbers to slide notes, tighten wording on KV cache.

[14:35] Jordan: Put Dedicated vs Hosted earlier and add one regulatory example for Private.

[14:41] Priya: Add a persona overlay and a one-line competitor positioning slide.

[14:47] Ravi: Add a short forward-looking line about Private roadmap — customers ask if air-gapped is on the roadmap. Don't promise timing, just 'in pilot with select partners'.

[14:58] Elena: I'll rewrite the opening to two variant scripts: 60s enterprise + 30s product-led. We'll circulate tomorrow.

[15:05] Aisha: Great. Final notes: remember to surface observability earlier — token-level dashboards, regression alerts, and fallbacks. Also, have the SLA numbers handy and an example anonymized cost-savings slide.

[15:22] (wrap)
[15:25] Aisha: Okay we'll capture action items; thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next Friday for mock calls with the new script.

[15:33] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional crosstalk and filler words removed for clarity in playback sections; original recording had two places with microphone hiss.
